grammarPoint.title: Each, every and all
grammarPoint.summary: Learn to use 'each', 'every', and 'all' to talk about all members of a group, focusing on individual items or the group as a whole.
grammarPoint.explanation:
We use *each*, *every*, and *all* to refer to all members of a group. While they all convey a sense of completeness, they are used differently depending on whether we are focusing on individuals or the group as a whole, and on the type of noun.

*Each* focuses on individual items within a group, one by one. It is always followed by a singular countable noun. For example, "Each participant received a badge." You can also use "each of the" before a plural noun or pronoun: "Each of the books was interesting."

*Every* refers to all members of a group as a whole, emphasizing completeness. It is also always followed by a singular countable noun. For example, "Every car needs fuel." Unlike 'each', 'every' cannot be directly followed by 'of the' + plural noun/pronoun (you would say "every one of the"). 'Every' usually implies a group of three or more.

*All* refers to the entire group, emphasizing the totality. It can be followed by plural countable nouns or uncountable nouns. For example, "All the students passed the exam" or "All the water evaporated." You can also use "all of the" before plural nouns, uncountable nouns, or pronouns: "All of the ingredients are fresh."
patterns: All of the + plural noun/uncountable noun/pronoun

examples.text: Each flower in the garden has a unique color.
examples.note: Focuses on individual flowers, one by one.

examples.text: Every employee attended the mandatory training session.
examples.note: Refers to all employees as a complete group.

examples.text: All the windows were cleaned before the party.
examples.note: Refers to the entire group of windows.

examples.text: All the equipment needs to be checked regularly.
examples.note: Refers to the entire amount of uncountable equipment.

examples.text: Each of the proposals was carefully reviewed by the committee.
examples.note: Highlights individual proposals from a larger group.

commonErrors.wrong: Every of the students passed the test.
commonErrors.right: Each of the students passed the test.
commonErrors.note: Use 'each of the' or 'every one of the' before a plural noun.
'Each' is followed by a singular countable noun.

commonErrors.wrong: All the student received a certificate.
commonErrors.right: All the students received a certificate.
commonErrors.note: 'All' with countable nouns is followed by a plural noun.

exercises.question: ___ participant received a small gift at the end of the conference.
exercises.explanation: 'Every' is used with a singular countable noun to refer to all members of a group.

exercises.question: ___ the ingredients are fresh, so the meal will be delicious.
exercises.explanation: 'All' is used with plural countable nouns like 'ingredients' to refer to the entire group.

exercises.question: The teacher spoke to ___ child individually about their progress.
exercises.explanation: 'Each' emphasizes individual members, which fits the idea of speaking to them 'individually'.

exercises.question: ___ the information you need is available on our website.
exercises.explanation: 'All' is used with uncountable nouns like 'information' to refer to the entire quantity.

exercises.text: ___ student in the class submitted their assignment on time.
exercises.explanation: 'Every' or 'Each' can be used here with a singular noun to refer to all students. 'Every' emphasizes the group, 'Each' emphasizes individuals.

exercises.text: ___ of the team members contributed to the project's success.
exercises.explanation: 'Each of the' focuses on individual members, while 'All of the' refers to the entire group. Both are grammatically correct here.

exercises.text: We checked ___ the doors and windows before leaving the house.
exercises.explanation: 'All' is used with plural countable nouns like 'doors and windows' to refer to the entire set.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: This sentence correctly uses 'each of the' with a plural noun and a singular verb to focus on individual flowers.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: This sentence correctly uses 'all the' with a plural noun to refer to the entire group of guests.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: Every of the books on the shelf is a classic.
answers: Each of the books on the shelf is a classic.
Every one of the books on the shelf is a classic.
exercises.explanation: 'Every' cannot be directly followed by 'of the'. Use 'each of the' or 'every one of the'.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: All the student must complete the final project.
answers: All the students must complete the final project.
Every student must complete the final project.
exercises.explanation: 'All' with countable nouns requires a plural noun. Alternatively, 'every' can be used with a singular noun.

exercises.source: Every person in the room agreed with the decision.
answers: All the people in the room agreed with the decision.
exercises.explanation: To use 'all', the singular noun 'person' must become the plural 'people', and 'the' is often used.

exercises.source: All the children received a small toy.
answers: Each child received a small toy.
Each of the children received a small toy.
exercises.explanation: When using 'each', the plural noun 'children' becomes the singular 'child'. 'Each of the' is also an option.
